newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria says it plans to reduce pollution.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria says it plans to reduce pollution.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said on Friday that it planned to reduce the negative impact of its operations on the Nigerian environment.

Egbert Imomoh, deputy managing director of the company, told a seminar on relations between oil companies and their host communities in the capital Abuja that measures aimed at ending gas flaring and spillages from pipelines, flowstations and export terminals were already in place.
The three-day seminar which began on Wednesday was attended by executives of oil multinationals, oil-producing communities leaders and state oil company oficials.
"Shell's new environmental programme aims to progressively reduce emmissions, effluents and discharges of wastes that have negative impact on the environment," said Imomoh.
Oil-producing communities often complain that the oil activities of the multinationals, including gas flaring, were damaging their environment and have been seeking compensations in return.
Imomoh said: "We are committed to putting our flares out by 2008, at the latest."

In January, Nigeria's military government gave oil companies a deadline of 2010 to stop gas flaring and in its 1997 fiscal budget, government offered incentives to oil companies to operate in its upstream sector and end the flaring of gas.

Imomoh said his company had the responsibility to quickly remedy a situation where a negative impact on the environmnet occurred, adding: "Compensation is paid to the affected communities except where sabotage is proven.
The oil companies sometimes accuse the oil-producing communities of deliberately causing spillages by vandalising their pipelines and machines.
Crude oil is the economic engine of Nigeria, accounting for slightly more than 90 percent of its foreign exchange earnings.
